the border trap distribution can be extracted from the C–V measurements at various temperatures based solely on the distributed border trap model.

the border traps are distributed in a Gaussian-like distribution with a peak at a depth of 2.5 nm from the interface, and the activation energy of the capture cross-section of these border traps is 0.25 eV.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the frequency dispersion of C–V characteristics in accumulation region at different temperatures can be used to extract the border traps distribution in space, which provides a new way to study the spatial distribution of oxide traps.
the border trap distribution can be obtained by fitting the experimental C–V data with the proposed model, and the fitting results agree well with those from the deep level transient spectroscopy.

the border trap distribution can be obtained from a single set of C–V measurements at various temperatures, rather than a series of C–V characteristics at a single temperature, which greatly facilitates the determination of border traps in InGaAs MOS structures.
